The petitioner is apprehending his arrest for the offences punishable under Sections
409/419/420 of the Indian Penal Code.
2.  Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner has been falsely implicated in the present case and has not committed any offence as alleged in the F.I.R.
The petitioner happened to be the 'Customer Associate' in SBI, Pandeydih Branch, Jamtara.

As per allegation, the Informant - Madan Kumar Choudhary (the present Branch Manager of the said Branch) was informed vide e-mail dated 14.02.2024 by one Tikait Chandra Das, the then Branch Manager of SBI, Pandeydih Branch that the petitioner had illegally withdrawn an amount of Rs.1,77,765/- in total on different dates from the bank accounts of the seven dead customers of the said branch.
It has further been alleged that the petitioner in his written reply dated 16.02.2024 has accepted his involvement in withdrawing the said amount, which has also been returned by him to the bank.
3. Learned counsel for the petitioner further submits that the petitioner is not at all involved in withdrawing the said amount from the bank accounts of the seven dead customers.

In fact, the petitioner has not admitted his involvement in the alleged offence, rather he was made to sign on blank paper by Tikait Chandra Das, the then Branch Manager of Pandeydih Branch, which was subsequently used as his acceptance of the said offence.

It is also submitted that Tikait Chandra Das was involved in tampering of important vouchers and documents in Pandeydih Branch and the said matter was communicated by the petitioner to the senior officials of the SBI through email on 08.02.2024.
The petitioner has been implicated in this case due to conspiracy hatched by Tikait Chandra Das.
Otherwise also, the amount said to have been withdrawn from the bank account of the seven dead customers has already been returned to the bank.
The petitioner also undertakes to Rajdeep Sonkar vs The State Of Jharkhand ... ...

Hence, he may be given the privilege of anticipatory bail.
4. Learned A.P.P opposes the petitioners' prayer for anticipatory bail.
5. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and considering the materials available on record, I am inclined to enlarge the petitioner on anticipatory bail.

Accordingly, the petitioner above named,
in the event of his arrest/surrender within three weeks from today, shall be released on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs.20,000/- (Rupees Twenty thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Jamtara, in connection with Narayanpur P.S. Case No. 39/2024, subject to the conditions as laid down under Section 482(2) of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.
